# v0.4.0 public launch preparation

Status: local acceptance passed, awaiting explicit maintainer approval. Target announcement: October 15, 2026. No release tag, GitHub release, push, or deployment is authorized by this record.

## Release decision for review

v0.4.0 is the first supported public baseline. Existing v0.2.x and v0.3.0 tags remain historical development artifacts; their APIs and stored shapes are not compatibility commitments. The current API and stored shapes become the baseline when the maintainer approves publication.

Settings, prototype metadata, contributor profiles, Canvas scenes, ownership maps, lockfiles, and public contract snapshots each use their current version-1 declaration. Version numbers identify each format independently. Contributor profiles use module preference namespaces. No contributor legacy-field mapping or v0.3.0 runtime-import conversion is shipped. Preference initialization adds current module defaults while preserving existing namespaces and custom data; it does not migrate development formats.

## Changes included

- API foundations: explicit execution environments; typed errors and mutation synchronization; owner routes and identity adapters; shared artifact inspection and hosting; module preference schemas; lazy build assets and application system services.
- Data protection: validated JSON snapshots reject accessors, declaration snapshots are isolated by physical file identity, subscriber failures are contained, and asset readers receive independent copies.
- Guidance: task-relevant context and skills, current installation and contribution instructions, and an explicit release approval requirement.
- Samples and distribution: fictional Parker Moss profile and offline avatar; permanent sample IDs retained; real maintainer profiles, private work, and personal grants excluded from distributed builds.
- Pre-launch cleanup: one current stored baseline, historical compatibility gate reset, and removal of obsolete preference migration and runtime repair machinery.

The detailed proposed release notes remain under `## Unreleased` in [CHANGELOG](../../CHANGELOG.md). Nothing in this record claims that the planned public tag is available.

## Final reliability acceptance

The maintainer dropped the full demo rehearsal in favor of using an existing system. Release acceptance still checks first-user behavior in disposable technical fixtures; it does not require the maintainer to repeat onboarding or system setup for the demo.

The final runtime candidate is `8b232e5bcc474178f8d8514e39c49f16d1ab74be`, including the canvas refinements and a first-visit onboarding fix. Welcome now waits for contributor identity before claiming its introduction. Previously, the loading identity could consume the server claim under an unregistered browser key, then close the dialog when the actual identity arrived. Regression coverage verifies both registered and unregistered readiness, request sharing, and persistence.

Acceptance ran on October 14, 2026 in `/tmp/design-studio-040-identity-acceptance`, a full-history clean clone with upstream `origin`, frozen dependencies, and no copied private content. This supersedes the earlier runtime baseline above.

| Check | Result | Local evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Sync, formatting, module checks, released contract, strict ownership, starter distribution | Passed | `/tmp/release-040-final-gates.log` |
| Full release regressions | 546 passed; no failures, cancellations, or skips; enabled control and all six optional modules disabled and removed passed | `/tmp/release-040-final-tests.log` |
| Actual update CLI | Synthetic 0.4.0 → 0.4.1 dry run, protected-content preservation, conflict/continue, frozen builds, and failed-check reporting passed | `/tmp/release-040-final-upgrade.log` |
| Production build and asset inspection | Passed; all manifest references exist; initial JS/CSS 715.1 KiB raw / 87.2 KiB gzip across two files; existing large-chunk warnings remain | `/tmp/release-040-final-gates.log` |
| Development import resolution | Passed separately with socket access; the full sandboxed suite had logged a denied WebSocket bind while passing this test | `/tmp/release-040-final-public-api-test.log` |
| Release dry run | Blocked only by local main differing from upstream main; no release files, tags, or publication changed | `/tmp/release-040-final-dry-run.log` |

A separate disposable browser fixture delayed `/__studio/me` by 1.5 seconds. The onboarding claim occurred after identity was released; the dialog remained interactive through all nine slides, completed, and stayed dismissed after reload. New prototype creation used the shipped Product system and retained its permanent artifact link after reload. This changed only a synthetic fixture contributor, not the maintainer's actual profile. Request timing is in `/tmp/release-040-browser-requests.log`; screenshots are `/tmp/release-040-welcome-delayed-identity.png` and `/tmp/release-040-first-prototype.png`.

The final clean production build rendered the sample document and native-text handoff canvas. Inbox filtering reduced eight data rows to three; direct-route reload restored eight. Dark mode rendered correctly and browser error logs were empty. Screenshots are `/tmp/release-040-final-handoff.png` and `/tmp/release-040-final-inbox-dark.png`. Disposable preview servers and browser tabs were stopped after verification. No additional engineering blocker was found within this acceptance scope. Exact public-tag installation and deployed-site checks remain pending publication authorization and the actual public tag.

## Canvas annotation refinement after acceptance

The maintainer requested native text instead of sticky notes on the Feedback Inbox engineering handoff canvas. All ten annotations now use native Excalidraw text, preserving their wording and the existing screen, arrow, section, link, and canvas identities and geometry. The Canvas skill, README, CLI help and examples, and Manual now prefer native text and drawing tools. The sticky note remains an optional example Library asset. Other canvases are unchanged.

The existing 22 Canvas tool tests, synchronization, module checks, formatting, and production build passed. Light and dark browser inspection passed on the local authoring preview. Logs are `/tmp/handoff-native-text-tests.log`, `/tmp/handoff-native-text-sync.log`, `/tmp/handoff-native-text-check.log`, `/tmp/handoff-native-text-format-check.log`, and `/tmp/handoff-native-text-build.log`; preview evidence is `/tmp/eng-handoff-native-text.png`. This refinement changes sample content and help text, not canvas editing or rendering behavior. The 544-test run above records the earlier runtime baseline, not a repeated full run after this content refinement. Publication remains on hold.

## Publication gates requiring maintainer attention

- Review the release scope, clean-baseline policy, proposed notes, and limitations, then explicitly direct publication.
- Candidate commits must reach upstream main and pass required CI before the real release dry run can pass. Pushing main also triggers public demo deployment, so preparation does not push it automatically.
- Update the website's install prompt and plain-text agent guide to the approved tag in coordination with publication. The live website currently targets v0.3.0. The prepared [website patch](v0.4.0-website.patch) updates both consumers in the separate website repository; apply it only in coordination with the approved public tag.
- After the exact tag is published, install from that public tag and verify a first prototype, fresh-session reopening, anonymous demo interactions, direct links, and reloads. Record exact commit, tag, CI and deployment URLs before announcement.

## Known limitations and deferred work

- Prior installation journeys used macOS, installed tools, existing accounts, and warm caches. Clean-computer and new-account installation are not verified claims.
- Plugin distribution, additional provider-specific hosting walkthroughs, and the existing-studio pilot remain deferred. Repository installation is the launch path.
- Large-chunk warnings and representative large-studio performance measurements remain performance follow-ups.
- Public viewing builds have no built-in sign-in. Hosting access controls and missing-asset behavior depend on the provider; GitHub Pages direct-route fallback responses retain HTTP 404 status.
- Inflight, DialKit, expanded design-system curation, and a creation video are outside this release's engineering gates.
